subject: AI & Agents
title: The Dartmouth Conference: AI Gets Its Name
description: Learn The Dartmouth Conference: AI Gets Its Name in one minute.

hook.text: In the summer of 1956, ten scientists gathered at Dartmouth College to create a new field.

buildup.text: John McCarthy coined the term 'artificial intelligence' for the workshop proposal.

discovery.text: Attendees believed that every aspect of learning could, in principle, be precisely described for a machine.

twist.text: They predicted human-level AI within a generation. Seven decades later, we're still working on it.

climax.text: But the conference launched research programs at MIT, Stanford, and Carnegie Mellon that shaped the field.

punchline.text: AI was born optimistic and overconfident.

details.summary: The 1956 Dartmouth Conference, organized by John McCarthy, coined the term 'artificial intelligence' and launched AI as a formal academic field. Early optimism predicted human-level AI within a generation.
details.whyItMatters: Dartmouth established AI as a discipline and set its ambitious agenda. The conference's overoptimistic predictions also set the pattern of hype and disillusionment that repeats to this day.
takeaways: The 1956 Dartmouth Conference coined artificial intelligence
It launched AI as a formal academic research field
Early predictions were wildly overoptimistic about AI timelines

faq.question: Who attended the Dartmouth Conference?
faq.answer: Founding figures including John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, and Allen Newell. These researchers shaped AI research for decades and founded leading AI labs at MIT, Stanford, and Carnegie Mellon.

faq.question: What did the organizers predict at Dartmouth?
faq.answer: They proposed that significant progress toward human-level AI could be made in one summer. This dramatic overestimation set a pattern of hype followed by disappointment that has repeated throughout AI history.
